frequency_question: How often do central banks enact temporary reserve ratio hikes within a specific 4-month operational window following liquidity surge periods?
membership_rule: Members are central banks in major emerging economies that introduced targeted secondary reserve requirements to mop up excess liquidity outside regular policy rate cycles. Excluded are standard statutory reserve ratio changes that occur as routine monetary policy updates.

cases.name: Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit adjustments
RBI iCRR equivalent historical liquidity absorptions

provenance_note: claims 15 cases from only 4 named (3.8x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 named reference cases from a broader estimated population of 15 similar liquidity overhang episodes in major emerging markets.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier market central banks with less transparent liquidity management frameworks.
skeleton: Central bank liquidity management interventions across major emerging markets subject to sudden capital inflows or government spending surges, evaluated over rolling 4-month observation windows.
multiplier: 4 distinct historical liquidity-absorption episodes identified in major emerging market jurisdictions over a 15-year observation frame yielding a base rate of occurrence.
validity_reason: Central bank liquidity management toolkits and structural monetary policy transmission mechanisms remain stable over a 5-year horizon.
